# Configuration reference

Every setting for the whole stack, generated from `terraform/variables.tf`.

**Do not edit this file.** `make docs` regenerates it and `make test` fails
when it is stale, so it always describes the variables as they actually are.

Settings go in `terraform/terraform.tfvars`, which is gitignored because the
Discord webhook URL in it is a credential. Copy `terraform.tfvars.example` to
start. Anything you leave out takes the default below.

```hcl
# terraform/terraform.tfvars
discord_public_key    = "..."          # required
accept_minecraft_eula = true           # required
idle_timeout_minutes  = 20             # anything else is optional
```

**Almost nothing here rebuilds the instance.** Terraform publishes these to one
SSM parameter which the instance re-reads on every boot, so `terraform apply`
followed by `/stop` and `/start` in Discord applies the change. The exceptions
are called out on the settings they apply to.

Related, with more context than a reference entry can carry:

- [What it costs](../README.md#what-it-costs) — which settings are free-tier bound
- [Route 53 setup](route53-setup.md) — the `route53_*` and `addressing_mode` settings
- [Mods](mods.md) — `server_mods`, and tuning the server for more players
- [Operations](operations.md) — applying changes, backups, upgrades

## Naming and placement

### `project_name`

`string` · default `"minecraft"`

Constraint: project_name must be lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 2-31 characters.

Prefix for every resource name. Use a different value to run more than one server in an account.

### `aws_region`

`string` · default `"us-west-2"`

Region to deploy into. Pick one close to your players; it is the single biggest lever on latency.

### `vpc_id`

`string` · default `""`

VPC to launch into. Leave empty to use the default VPC for the account.

### `subnet_id`

`string` · default `""`

Subnet to launch into. Leave empty to pick the first default subnet in the VPC. Must be a public subnet.

### `tags`

`map(string)` · default `{}`

Extra tags applied to every resource.


## Compute

### `instance_type`

`string` · default `"t4g.small"`

EC2 instance type. Graviton (t4g) is roughly 20% cheaper than the x86
equivalent and runs Fabric fine; the architecture and AMI are selected
automatically from whatever you put here.

The default is free-tier eligible: t4g.small is covered by the T4g free
trial (750 hours a month, every account, through 31 December 2026) and is
also on the free-tier list for accounts opened on or after 15 July 2025.
It is the smallest type that runs a Minecraft server at all -- the micro
types in the free tier have 1 GB of memory, which the JVM cannot work in.

Rough guide: t4g.small (2 GB) for 2-3 players on a light world,
t4g.medium (4 GB) for up to about 8, t4g.large (8 GB) for a modpack.
Anything above t4g.small is billed at the normal on-demand rate.

Changing size within a family is applied in place. Changing architecture
(t4g -> t3) on a deployment that already exists needs
`terraform apply -replace=aws_instance.server`, because the AMI is pinned
after the first boot and the old one would not boot on the new CPU. The
world is on its own volume either way.

### `root_volume_gb`

`number` · default `8`

Root volume size. Holds the OS and the scripts only; the world lives on the
data volume. Amazon Linux, Java and Node come to about 4 GB.

The default plus data_volume_gb is 28 GB, which fits the 30 GB of EBS the
free tier covers. Raising either past that budget starts a monthly charge.

### `data_volume_gb`

`number` · default `20`

Persistent volume for the world, backups and mods. Survives instance
replacement. Counts against the same 30 GB free-tier EBS budget as
root_volume_gb.

### `server_mods`

`list(string)` · default `["lithium", "ferrite-core", "krypton"]`

Constraint: Each server_mods entry must be a Modrinth slug, slug@version, or an https:// URL ending in .jar.

Fabric mods to install, reconciled against the mods directory on every
boot: entries added here are downloaded, entries removed are deleted, and a
Minecraft version change re-resolves all of them.

Each entry is a Modrinth project slug, a slug pinned to one build
(`lithium@0.15.0`), or an https URL ending in .jar for anything not on
Modrinth. Jars copied into the directory by hand are never touched.

The default three are server-side only, need no Fabric API and require
nothing of players' clients. They are what makes the free-tier t4g.small
hold more than a couple of people:

  lithium      rewrites the hot paths of the game tick. The single
               biggest win, and behaviour-preserving.
  ferrite-core cuts heap use substantially, which on a 2 GB instance is
               the difference between headroom and garbage-collection
               pauses.
  krypton      lighter networking, mostly felt with several players
               loading chunks at once.

A mod with no build for the running Minecraft version is skipped, and its
jar removed if one was installed for an older version -- Fabric refuses to
start rather than run a mismatched mod. Set this to [] to run vanilla.

### `java_heap_mb`

`number` · default `0`

Java heap size in MB. 0 sizes it from the memory of the instance, leaving 1 GB for the OS.

### `java_package`

`string` · default `"java-21-amazon-corretto-headless"`

JDK package to install. Minecraft 1.20.5 and later need Java 21.


## Addressing

### `addressing_mode`

`string` · default `"elastic_ip"`

Accepted values: `elastic_ip`, `route53`, `none`

How players reach the server, given the public IP changes on every boot.

  elastic_ip - attach a static IP. No domain needed. Costs about $3.60 a
               month for the hours the instance is stopped; free while it
               is running.
  route53    - the boot script repoints an A record at the new IP. Needs a
               hosted zone you control. No idle charge.
  none       - players read the raw IP from /status each session.

### `route53_zone_id`

`string` · default `""`

Hosted zone ID. Required when addressing_mode is route53.

### `route53_record_name`

`string` · default `""`

Fully qualified name for the A record, for example mc.example.com. Required when addressing_mode is route53.

### `route53_ttl`

`number` · default `30`

TTL for the A record. Keep it short so a restart propagates quickly.

### `server_port`

`number` · default `25565`

Port the server listens on.

### `allowed_cidrs`

`list(string)` · default `["0.0.0.0/0"]`

CIDR blocks allowed to reach the Minecraft port. Narrow this if you know which networks your players are on.

### `enable_ssh`

`bool` · default `false`

Open port 22. Off by default: SSM Session Manager gives you a shell with no open port and no key to lose.

### `ssh_key_name`

`string` · default `""`

Existing EC2 key pair name, used only when enable_ssh is true.

### `ssh_allowed_cidrs`

`list(string)` · default `[]`

CIDR blocks allowed to reach port 22 when enable_ssh is true.


## Discord

### `discord_public_key`

`string` · **required**

Constraint: discord_public_key must be the 64-character hex key from the Discord developer portal.

Public key from the General Information page of the Discord application. Used to verify interaction signatures.

### `discord_webhook_url`

`string` · default `""` · sensitive — kept out of Terraform output

Channel webhook the server posts status messages to. Leave empty to disable notifications.

### `discord_bot_username`

`string` · default `"Minecraft Server"`

Display name on webhook messages.

### `allow_stop_command`

`bool` · default `true`

Whether /stop is available at all.

Set this to false on a shared server and the only way it powers off is by
going idle: nobody can end a session other people are still in, whether by
accident or to be a nuisance. The command stays registered in Discord and
replies explaining how long the server waits when empty, rather than
failing silently.

This is enforced in two places. The Lambda refuses the command, and with
stop disabled Terraform also declines to grant the Lambda the
ssm:SendCommand permission that carries it out, so the capability is not
merely hidden.

An operator can still stop the server from a shell on the instance
(`sudo mc stop`), which is the intended escape hatch.

### `discord_stop_role_ids`

`list(string)` · default `[]`

Discord role IDs allowed to run /stop, when it is enabled. Empty means
anyone who may use the other commands may also stop the server.

Use this instead of allow_stop_command = false when you want the people
running the server to keep the button and everybody else not to have it.
Roles listed here still have to pass discord_allowed_role_ids, if that is
set.

### `discord_allowed_role_ids`

`list(string)` · default `[]`

Discord role IDs allowed to run the commands. Empty means everyone in the server may.


## Minecraft

### `accept_minecraft_eula`

`bool` · default `false`

Constraint: You must accept the Minecraft EULA by setting accept_minecraft_eula = true.

Set to true to accept the Minecraft EULA (https://aka.ms/MinecraftEULA). The server will not start otherwise.

### `minecraft_version`

`string` · default `"latest"`

Minecraft version, or latest for the newest stable release Fabric supports.

### `fabric_loader_version`

`string` · default `"latest"`

Fabric loader version, or latest for the newest stable one.

### `server_jar_url`

`string` · default `""`

Direct download URL for a server jar. Set this to run Paper, Purpur or vanilla instead of Fabric; it overrides the version settings above.

### `idle_timeout_minutes`

`number` · default `15`

Minutes with no players before the server saves, backs up and powers the instance off.

### `max_uptime_hours`

`number` · default `0`

Hard cap on a single session, as a runaway-cost guard. 0 disables it.

### `shutdown_on_crash`

`bool` · default `true`

Power the instance off if the server exits unexpectedly, so a crash cannot quietly bill for hours. Turn off while debugging.

### `server_motd`

`string` · default `"An on-demand Minecraft server"`

Message shown in the multiplayer server list.

### `server_difficulty`

`string` · default `"normal"`

Accepted values: `peaceful`, `easy`, `normal`, `hard`

peaceful, easy, normal or hard.

### `server_gamemode`

`string` · default `"survival"`

Accepted values: `survival`, `creative`, `adventure`, `spectator`

survival, creative, adventure or spectator.

### `server_max_players`

`number` · default `10`

Player slots.

### `server_view_distance`

`number` · default `10`

View distance in chunks. Lowering this is the cheapest way to help a small instance keep up.

### `server_simulation_distance`

`number` · default `10`

Simulation distance in chunks.

### `server_online_mode`

`bool` · default `true`

Require Mojang authentication. Leave this true unless you know exactly why you are turning it off.

### `server_whitelist`

`bool` · default `false`

Enable the whitelist. Strongly recommended when the port is open to the internet.

### `server_ops`

`list(string)` · default `[]`

Minecraft usernames to make operators on a fresh install. Ignored once ops.json exists.

### `server_whitelist_players`

`list(string)` · default `[]`

Minecraft usernames to seed the whitelist with on a fresh install.


## Backups

### `backup_retention_days`

`number` · default `30`

Days to keep backups in S3 before they expire. 0 keeps them forever.

### `local_backup_keep`

`number` · default `3`

Number of recent backups to also keep on the data volume for a fast restore.

### `restore_from_s3`

`string` · default `""`

s3://bucket/key of a backup tarball to unpack on first boot. Use this to migrate an existing world.

### `force_destroy_buckets`

`bool` · default `false`

Allow terraform destroy to delete the S3 bucket while it still holds backups.

### `cpu_credits`

`string` · default `"standard"`

Accepted values: `standard`, `unlimited`

Burstable CPU mode for t3/t4g instances.

  standard  - predictable bill. The server may stutter during world
              generation or when several players explore at once.
  unlimited - smooth under load, at roughly $0.05 per extra vCPU-hour.

Only applied when the instance type is burstable.
